item: What type(s) of genetic testing have you had? Please select all that apply.
item_detail: Chromosomes (Also called chromosome analysis, karyotype, karyotype analysis, or G-band karyotype) / Direct-to-consumer (DTC) genetic test (Genetic testing that is ordered by and returned directly to the person tested rather than through a doctor, also called DTC; please specify name of the company and/or test below) / Single gene or gene panel test (Testing of ONE or MULTIPLE genes with a single test; please specify the name of the test or condition being tested for below) / Microarray (Also called chromosomal microarray, CMA, cytogenomic array, array, or array CGH) / Exome sequencing (Testing that targets a person’s complete set of genes; also called whole exome sequencing or WES) / Genome sequencing (Testing of a person’s complete DNA sequence, including genes and regions between them; also called whole genome sequencing or WGS) / Unsure
proposed_note: Adds a repeat expansion test and mitochondrial DNA testing, then asks which sample was tested, what the result said, the gene if known, and about reanalysis.

item: What was the reason for your genetic testing?
item_detail: I have had symptoms of a genetic condition. / The doctor/I wanted to confirm a diagnosis that was suspected based on my symptoms. / I have a family history of a genetic disorder and was showing symptoms of that disorder – wanted to confirm diagnosis. / I have a family history of a genetic disorder and was NOT showing symptoms of the disorder – wanted to assess my risk. I am healthy and wanted to be proactive about my health. / Unsure
proposed_note: Separates family history without symptoms from being proactive while healthy, and adds family planning.

item: Do you have a copy of your genetic test result(s)?

item: 1. Have you been told that there were issues during your biological mother's PREGNANCY with you and/or your DELIVERY/BIRTH?
item_detail: Examples: Mother had to be put on bed rest, there were concerns on ultrasound, you were born early (prematurely), or you had to stay in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU).
proposed_note: Asked as: Before and around birth. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 2. Have you had issues with your GROWTH?
item_detail: Examples: You are much shorter or taller than expected for your family, you have had significant and/or lifelong problems gaining weight, or you have significant and/or lifelong problems with obesity. You may have seen an endocrinologist or other specialist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Growth and weight. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 3. Have you had issues with your HORMONES and/or ENDOCRINE SYSTEM (hormone-producing glands)?
item_detail: Examples: Diabetes, issues with estrogen or testosterone levels, or function of the thyroid, parathyroid, or adrenal glands. You may have seen an endocrinologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Hormones, glands, and metabolism. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 4. Have you ever been diagnosed with cancer?
item_detail: Examples: Breast cancer, prostate cancer, osteosarcoma, lymphoma, etc. You may have seen an oncologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Cancer and tumors. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 5. Have you had issues with your HEAD/FACE/NECK?
item_detail: Please note that we are asking you about SIGNIFICANT issues with these areas, problems that you have seen a doctor for or had surgery for, or problems that you don't notice often in other people. The doctor may have used the term “dysmorphic” in describing some features of your face. Examples: Cleft lip/palate, large or small head size, fused skull bones, sparse hair, etc. We will ask specifically about eyes and ears later.
proposed_note: Asked as: Head, face, and neck. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 6. Have you had issues with your EYES and/or VISION?
item_detail: Examples: Vision loss, cataracts, a “lazy eye,” nearsighted- or farsightedness. You may have seen an optometrist or ophthalmologist (eye doctors) for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Eyes and vision. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 7. Have you had issues with your EARS and/or HEARING?
item_detail: Examples: Hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or misshapen ears. You may have seen an audiologist or Ears/Nose/Throat (ENT) doctor for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Ears and hearing. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 8. Have you had issues with BRAIN and/or NERVOUS SYSTEM (neurological issues)?
item_detail: Examples: Developmental delays, intellectual disability, learning problems, seizures, significant problems with muscle tone, cerebral palsy, or problems with brain structure. You may have seen a neurologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Brain and nerves. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 9. Have you had BEHAVIOR and/or PSYCHIATRIC issues?
item_detail: Examples: Autism spectrum disorders, schizophrenia, anxiety, aggression, repetitive behaviors, and depression. You may have seen a developmental pediatrician, psychologist, psychiatrist, or therapist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Thinking, mood, and behavior. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 10. Have you had issues with your SKIN?
item_detail: Examples: Unusual skin coloration, lumps or bumps that needed to be looked at by a doctor, or sweating issues. You may have seen a dermatologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Skin, hair, and nails. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 11. Have you had issues with your BONES, CARTILAGE, and/or CONNECTIVE TISSUE?
item_detail: Examples: Issues with easily broken bones, extreme flexibility, or the look/use of your arms, legs, hands, and/or feet. You may have seen an orthopedist or other special doctor for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Bones, joints, and chest. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 12. Have you had issues with your MUSCLES?
item_detail: Examples: Significant issues with the way your muscles are formed or the way they work, including muscle weakness, burning, or stiffness. You may have seen a neurologist, orthopedist, or other special doctor for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Muscles and strength. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 13. Have you had issues with your HEART and/or BLOOD VESSELS?
item_detail: Examples: Cardiomyopathy, heart defects needing surgery, widened/bulging blood vessel, or problems with heart rhythm. You may have seen a cardiologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Heart and blood vessels. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 14. Have you had issues with your LUNGS and/or BREATHING?
item_detail: Examples: A collapsed lung, fluid on the lungs, or apnea. You may have seen a pulmonologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Lungs and breathing. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 15. Have you had issues with your DIGESTIVE SYSTEM?
item_detail: Examples: Includes stomach, intestines, or other parts of gastrointestinal (GI) tract. Examples: Issues with the structure or use of your stomach or intestines, extreme issues with constipation, reflux, and/or vomiting. You may have seen a GI (gastrointestinal) doctor for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Digestion and feeding. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 16. Have you had issues with your KIDNEYS, BLADDER, and/or GENITALS (male/female reproductive parts)?
item_detail: Examples: Issues with urination, kidneys, or reproductive system, including concerns about how these body parts look or work. Some specific examples are hypospadias, kidney failure, infertility, and incontinence. You may have seen a nephrologist, urologist, gynecologist, or other special doctor for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Kidneys, bladder, and genitals. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 17. Have you had issues with your IMMUNE SYSTEM?
item_detail: Examples: Frequent infections or immunodeficiency. You may have seen an immunologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Immune system. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 18. Have you had issues with your BLOOD and/or BLEEDING?
item_detail: Examples: Excessive bleeding or problems noted with your blood cells on lab reports. You may have seen a hematologist for these issues.
proposed_note: Asked as: Blood and bleeding. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: 19. Have you had issues with your ORAL HEALTH?
proposed_note: Asked as: Mouth and teeth. Yes and Not sure both open the detail page.

item: If the following surgical procedures were used to treat seizures, select the status, outcome and the age of diagnosis. (Select all that apply.)

The device detects abnormal electrical activity and sends an electrical current. / Lobectomy/Lobe resection - The largest part of the brain (cerebrum) is divided into four sections (frontal, parietal, occipital, and temporal lobes). Lobectomy/ lobe resection involves removing a lobe of the brain. / Lesionectomy - Removal of the brain tissue that causes seizures such as a tumor or malformed blood vessel. / Hempispherectomy - Removal of a cerebral hemisphere. / Corpus callostomy - The corpus callosum is a band of nerve fibers connecting the two halves of the brain.
